papers.title: AI/ML for Network Security: The Emperor has no Clothes (Trustee)
papers.authors: Arthur S. Jacobs, Roman Beltiukov, Walter Willinger, Ronaldo A. Ferreira, Arpit Gupta, Lisandro Z. Granville
papers.relevance: Trustee extracts global decision-tree explanations plus a 'trust report' from any black-box network-security ML model and uses them to expose shortcut learning, spurious correlations, and out-of-distribution fragility in published traffic-analysis models - the central credibility critique that motivates XAI for traffic classification.

papers.title: Interpreting Deep Learning-Based Networking Systems (Metis)
papers.authors: Zili Meng, Minhu Wang, Jiasong Bai, Mingwei Xu, Hongzi Mao, Hongxin Hu
papers.relevance: Metis converts DNN policies in networking systems into interpretable controllers via teacher-student decision-tree distillation (local control, e.g. congestion control/flow scheduling) and hypergraph formulations (global control), with four use cases on how operators design, debug, deploy and adjust DL-based network systems - the canonical 'self-driving network explainability' paper.

papers.title: EXPLORA: AI/ML EXPLainability for the Open RAN
papers.authors: Claudio Fiandrino, Leonardo Bonati, Salvatore D'Oro, Michele Polese, Tommaso Melodia, Joerg Widmer
papers.relevance: Synthesizes network-oriented explanations of DRL xApps via an attributed graph linking agent actions to input state, prototyped on an O-RAN near-RT RIC over the Colosseum emulator; explanation-driven intent-based action steering yields ~4% median bitrate gains - flagship XAI-for-RAN-control work.

papers.title: AIChronoLens: Advancing Explainability for Time Series AI Forecasting in Mobile Networks
papers.authors: Claudio Fiandrino, Eloy Perez Gomez, Pablo Fernandez Perez, Hossein Mohammadalizadeh, Marco Fiore, Joerg Widmer
papers.relevance: Ties legacy XAI relevance scores to temporal properties (maxima/minima) of the input so explanations of LSTM/transformer traffic-load forecasters for 5G base stations become meaningful; explanation-guided retraining improves prediction error by 32% (39% with meta-learning) on real operator traces.

papers.title: Spotting Deep Neural Network Vulnerabilities in Mobile Traffic Forecasting with an Explainable AI Lens (DeExp)
papers.authors: Serly Moghadas Gholian, Claudio Fiandrino, Alan Collet, Giulia Attanasio, Marco Fiore, Joerg Widmer
papers.relevance: Uses Grad-CAM and Layer-wise Relevance Propagation to find which base stations a mobile-traffic-forecasting DNN depends on, showing prediction error grows >400% under moderate adversarial traffic injection - XAI as a vulnerability-audit tool for operational forecasting models.

papers.title: SymbXRL: Symbolic Explainable Deep Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Networks
papers.authors: Abhishek Duttagupta, Claudio Fiandrino, et al.
papers.relevance: Synthesizes human-interpretable symbolic explanations (symbols + logical rules) for DRL agents managing 6G resource allocation, and uses them for intent-based programmatic action steering that improves cumulative reward by ~12% over pure DRL.

papers.title: EXPLAIN-IT: Towards Explainable AI for Unsupervised Network Traffic Analysis
papers.authors: Andrea Morichetta, Pedro Casas, Marco Mellia
papers.relevance: Brings LIME-style explanations to unsupervised clustering of unlabeled traffic and demonstrates it on YouTube video-quality (QoE) classification under encryption - the earliest dedicated XAI-for-QoE-monitoring methodology.

papers.title: XAInomaly: Explainable and interpretable Deep Contractive Autoencoder for O-RAN traffic anomaly detection
papers.authors: Osman Tugay Basaran, Falko Dressler
papers.relevance: Semi-supervised deep contractive autoencoder for O-RAN traffic anomaly detection paired with fastSHAP-C, a resource-aware SHAP variant designed for real-time explanation inside near-RT RIC constraints - representative of the 'lightweight XAI for 6G' thread.

papers.title: SliceOps: Explainable MLOps for Streamlined Automation-Native 6G Networks
papers.authors: Farhad Rezazadeh, Sarang Kahvazadeh, et al.
papers.relevance: Embeds an XAI-augmented MLOps loop ('SliceOps') as a standalone slice in 6G architecture, using explanation-guided reinforcement learning for radio resource allocation across slices - joins the XAI and MLOps lifecycles for slicing automation.

papers.title: Explanation-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning for Trustworthy 6G RAN Slicing
papers.authors: Farhad Rezazadeh, Hatim Chergui, Luis Alonso, Christos Verikoukis
papers.relevance: Uses explanations inside the DRL training loop (explanation-guided reward) for multi-agent inter-slice resource allocation so SLA-meeting slicing decisions stay transparent, directly addressing the opaqueness objection to DRL slice controllers.

papers.title: TEFL: Turbo Explainable Federated Learning for 6G Trustworthy Zero-Touch Network Slicing
papers.authors: Swastika Roy, Hatim Chergui, Christos Verikoukis
papers.relevance: Closed-loop 'explanation-aware' federated learning for zero-touch slice SLA prediction where Integrated Gradients/SHAP attributions feed a confidence metric constraining training under non-IID data - XAI as an in-the-loop constraint, not post-hoc decoration.

papers.title: Toward Explainable Reasoning in 6G: A Proof of Concept Study on Radio Resource Allocation (TANGO)
papers.authors: Farhad Rezazadeh, et al.
papers.venue: arXiv (IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society version)
papers.relevance: Couples graph reinforcement learning with a Bayesian-GNN explainer and symbolic reasoning that translates edge/node importance and uncertainty into logical reward terms for gNodeB resource allocation, reporting 96.39% accuracy and 1.22x gains over baselines.

papers.title: LEAD-Drift: Real-time and Explainable Intent Drift Detection by Learning a Data-Driven Risk Score
papers.authors: Md. Kamrul Hossain, et al.
papers.relevance: Neural risk score for intent drift in Intent-Based Networking with SHAP-based per-alert explanations that identify root-cause KPIs, achieving 7.3-minute average lead time and 80.2% alert-noise reduction - joins explainability with operational root-cause analysis.

papers.title: BEAR: BGP Event Analysis and Reporting
papers.authors: Hanqing Li, et al.
papers.relevance: LLM-based multi-step reasoning that turns tabular BGP telemetry into explanatory natural-language reports for anomalies such as route leaks and hijacks - the emerging 'LLM as explainer' pattern for network operations, including a synthetic data generation framework.

papers.title: ExplainIt! - A Declarative Root-cause Analysis Engine for Time Series Data
papers.authors: Vimalkumar Jeyakumar, Omid Madani, Ali Parandeh, Ashutosh Kulshreshtha, Weifei Zeng, Navindra Yadav
papers.relevance: Unsupervised, declarative (SQL-like) root-cause analysis engine over datacenter/network telemetry time series from Cisco Tetration, letting operators rank thousands of causal hypotheses - explainable RCA at production scale.

papers.title: An Explainable AI-based Intrusion Detection System for DNS over HTTPS (DoH) Attacks
papers.authors: Tahmina Zebin, Shahadate Rezvy, Yuan Luo
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security (vol. 17, pp. 2339-2349)
papers.relevance: Balanced stacked random forest over the CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 dataset detects malicious DoH tunneling with ~99.9% F1, with SHAP values showing per-feature impact on decisions - the reference XAI paper for encrypted-DNS fingerprinting/detection.

papers.title: TunnelEye: An Explainable Framework for Real-Time Detection of Malicious DoH Traffic in High-Speed Backbone Networks
papers.authors: Jiajia Du, et al.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
papers.relevance: Argues existing DoH detectors' generic bidirectional statistics 'lack interpretability, are costly to compute, and may become unavailable or unstable' under backbone sampling; proposes protocol-level behavioral features stable across directions plus a DoH-Sketch data structure for real-time explainable detection.

papers.title: Machine Learning Interpretability Meets TLS Fingerprinting
papers.authors: Mahdi Jafari Siavoshani, Amir Hossein Khajepour, Amirmohammad Ziaei, Amir Ali Gatmiri, Ali Taheri
papers.relevance: Uses ML interpretation techniques to systematically locate the most information-leaking fields of the TLS protocol (handshake, record length, IV) from fingerprinting attacks over 70+ domains - interpretability as a protocol-auditing instrument for encrypted-traffic fingerprinting.

papers.title: Examining the Rat in the Tunnel: Interpretable Multi-Label Classification of Tor-based Malware
papers.authors: Ishan Karunanayake, et al.
papers.relevance: Message-passing neural network classifies Tor-based malware traffic (micro-avg precision/recall >90%) and applies XAI to interpret which traffic patterns distinguish malware classes, plus an adversarial-robustness evaluation - malware-over-anonymity-network detection with explanations.

papers.title: TrafficAV: An effective and explainable detection of mobile malware behavior using network traffic
papers.authors: Shanshan Wang, Zhenxiang Chen, et al.
papers.relevance: Early (2016) system explicitly marketed as 'explainable' mobile-malware detection from network traffic, pairing detection with human-meaningful analysis of why an app's traffic is flagged - a seminal precursor of explainable malware-traffic detection.

papers.title: RADAR: A TTP-based Extensible, Explainable, and Effective System for Network Traffic Analysis and Malware Detection

papers.relevance: Grounds malware detection from traffic in MITRE ATT&CK TTPs so every alert is explainable in analyst vocabulary rather than opaque model scores - explainability-by-domain-semantics for malware traffic analysis.

papers.authors: Sileshi Nibret Zeleke, et al.
papers.relevance: Ensemble (XGBoost, 99.32% acc.) over multi-view features of encrypted malicious traffic (custom 1,127-connection dataset spanning 54 malware families, benchmarked on CTU-13) with SHAP identifying max packet size, mean inter-arrival time and TLS version as decisive features.

papers.authors: Shayan Azizi, et al.
papers.relevance: Explicitly positions service-level IoT device identification as 'macroscopic, lightweight, and explainable' versus packet-level deep learning, validated on 13 consumer IoT device types over 10M IPFIX flow records spanning 1.5 years - interpretable-by-design device fingerprinting.

papers.authors: Cristian Zilli, et al.

papers.title: Explainable AI in 6G O-RAN: A Tutorial and Survey on Architecture, Use Cases, Challenges, and Future Research
papers.authors: Bouziane Brik, Hatim Chergui, Lanfranco Zanzi, Francesco Devoti, Adlen Ksentini, Muhammad Shuaib Siddiqui, Xavier Costa-Perez, Christos Verikoukis
papers.venue: arXiv tutorial/survey (IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials version exists)
papers.relevance: Tutorial-survey on deploying XAI inside O-RAN RIC control loops (xApps/rApps), covering automated XAI pipelines and security of explanations - the most operationally concrete of the 6G XAI surveys.

papers.title: Robust and Reliable Early-Stage Website Fingerprinting Attacks via Spatial-Temporal Distribution Analysis (Holmes)

papers.title: Measuring Information Leakage in Website Fingerprinting Attacks and Defenses (WeFDE)

papers.authors: Irena Orsolic, Dario Pevec, Mirko Suznjevic, Lea Skorin-Kapov
papers.relevance: Operator-side YouTube QoE classification from encrypted traffic with explicit feature analysis of which traffic-level features carry QoE information - foundational interpretable-ML line for in-network QoE monitoring.

recurring_datasets: CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 (DoH attack detection - Zebin et al.)
CTU-13 plus small custom malware captures (Zeleke: 1,127 connections, 54 families)
Colosseum O-RAN emulator / O-RAN-compliant near-RT RIC testbeds (EXPLORA, slicing XRL papers)
Real operator mobile-traffic traces, often unreleased (AIChronoLens, DeExp/INFOCOM'23, TelcoAgent: 200-cell city-scale 5G)
Tor WF corpora in the Rimmer/Sirinam lineage; WeFDE's 211,219 visits to ~2,200 sites; Holmes' six datasets incl. dark-web
Streaming-video sessions of Netflix/YouTube/Amazon/Twitch (Bronzino: 66 homes / 16 months; Orsolic: lab YouTube captures)
IoT testbeds: 13 consumer device types, 10M IPFIX flows over 1.5 years (Azizi et al.)
recurring_explanation_methods: SHAP is overwhelmingly dominant, including efficiency variants (fastSHAP-C in XAInomaly) and in-training uses (TEFL confidence constraint, LEAD-Drift per-alert root-cause KPIs, Holmes stage-wise feature importance, Zeleke)
Decision-tree surrogates / distillation for global explanation (Trustee, Metis teacher-student, O-RAN DT verifiers; NetPoirot and Bronzino use trees/interpretable features natively)
Gradient/backprop attributions: Grad-CAM and LRP (DeExp INFOCOM'23), Integrated Gradients (TEFL)
Graph/symbolic explanation of DRL agents: attributed graphs (EXPLORA), symbolic rules + logical reasoning (SymbXRL, TANGO, DeRAN-style distillation)
Information-theoretic feature-leakage measurement as interpretability (WeFDE mutual information; TLS-fingerprinting leaky-field analysis)
LLM-generated natural-language explanations/reports (BEAR for BGP; NOMS'25 LLM anomaly explanation)
recurring_models_being_explained: DRL agents (DQN/PPO/multi-agent) for RAN slicing, scheduling and resource allocation - the single most common explanandum in the ops literature
CNN/LSTM/transformer time-series forecasters of mobile traffic load and KPIs
Tree ensembles (RF/XGBoost/stacked RF) for DoH, malware and QoE tasks
CNNs on packet/trace representations for website fingerprinting; MPNN/GNNs for Tor malware and radio-resource graphs
author_stated_limitations_and_future_wor: Trustee (CCS'22): published network-security ML models routinely exhibit underspecification - 'evidence of shortcut learning, presence of spurious correlations, and vulnerability to out-of-distribution samples' - i.e., the models being explained are often not learning the intended phenomenon at all.

TunnelEye (TNSM'26): prior DoH detectors' features 'lack interpretability, are costly to compute, and may become unavailable or unstable in backbone monitoring nodes with massive unidirectional and sampled traffic' - stated as the gap motivating their design.
ClearNET (TNSM'25): 'the use of these [XAI] techniques in computer network management remains largely unexplored' - field-level immaturity acknowledged by authors in 2025.

DeExp / INFOCOM'23 (Moghadas Gholian et al.): forecasting DNNs are 'complex black boxes... proven vulnerable to adversarial attacks which undermine their applicability in production networks'; error grows >400% under moderate injection; different XAI methods disagree by regime (Grad-CAM for moderate/low, LRP for high traffic injection) - method-choice sensitivity is itself a limitation.
WFCAT (arXiv 2412.11487): residual 'performance degradation under certain defenses indicates room for further robustness improvements'.
Karunanayake et al. (2409.16639): adversarial vulnerability of the interpretable MPNN classifier 'remains a concern for deployment'.
Zeleke et al. (2501.05387): custom dataset is small (1,127 unique connections), a scale limitation typical of encrypted-malware XAI studies.
XAInomaly (Comput. Netw. 2025): standard SHAP is too heavy for near-RT RIC latency budgets, forcing a custom fastSHAP-C approximation - real-time constraints on XAI are an explicit open problem.
TEFL (2210.10147): explanation faithfulness must be validated under non-IID federated data; attribution-based confidence is their proxy, acknowledged as imperfect.
EXPLAIN-IT (2003.01670): presented as a methodology with the YouTube QoE use case; quantitative validation of explanation quality left open ('no ground truth for explanations' problem).

Bronzino et al. (SIGMETRICS'20): finding that 'higher internet speeds provide only minimal improvements to startup delay and resolution'; model retraining needed as services evolve - concept drift in QoE models.

eXplaNet (2509.21649) and the RL-XAI thread: authors frame XAI-for-networking-RL as 'opportunities and challenges' - no standard faithfulness metrics, explanations mostly post-hoc, steering via explanations still heuristic.
Cui et al. WF survey (2510.11804): open challenges include multi-tab browsing, coarse-grained features, and the accuracy-vs-interpretability trade-off between classical ML and DL for WF.
Brik et al. O-RAN survey (2307.00319): automating XAI pipelines inside RIC control loops and securing the explanations themselves (XAI as attack surface) are listed as future research.

Wang et al. 6G XAI survey (2112.04698): risk of 'high-speed, data-intensive AI decision-making beyond designers' and users' comprehension'; XAI-performance trade-off unresolved for real-time 6G loops.
Sim-to-real gap: nearly all O-RAN/slicing XAI validation is on emulators (Colosseum) or simulators, not production RANs - acknowledged across EXPLORA and follow-ups.
search_observations: Website fingerprinting + XAI has surprisingly little dedicated literature: interpretability appears either as information-theoretic feature analysis (WeFDE), as a design tool inside attacks (Holmes' stage-wise SHAP), or in surveys - a genuine gap for the survey to note.
No dedicated QUIC-fingerprinting XAI paper surfaced; closest are TLS-field leakage interpretation (2011.06304) and AutoML QUIC WF without explanations - another citable gap.

The IMDEA Networks group (Fiandrino/Fiore/Widmer) and the Rezazadeh/Chergui/Verikoukis cluster together account for a large share of mobile-network XAI output (EXPLORA, AIChronoLens, DeExp, SymbXRL; SliceOps, TEFL, TANGO).
